titulo: Si + present indicative, then present or future
subtitulo: Si hay olas, voy / iré: real conditions about the future.
regla: For a likely condition: si + present, then present or future. Never si + present subjunctive or si + future.

bloques.texto: To say that something will probably happen if a condition is met, a condition with a **high chance**, use **si** (_if_) + the **present**, then the **present** or the **future**.
Present or future in the main part doesn't change the meaning: **si me concentro, termino pronto** = **si me concentro, terminaré pronto**.
The order can flip: **hablaré con tu profe si tenemos dudas**.
**Si** is never followed by the present subjunctive, and never by the future: **si llueve**, not **si llueva** or **si lloverá**.
Tip: after **si**, keep it plain and present. The future waits on the other side of the comma.

lista.en: If I concentrate, I'll finish the job soon.
If I concentrate, I'll finish the job soon.

lista.es: Si Beto ==va== al mercado, ==compra== pescado fresco.
lista.en: If Beto goes to the market, he'll buy fresh fish.

lista.es: Si ==hay== olas mañana, ==iremos== a Baja Malibú.
lista.en: If there are waves tomorrow, we'll go to Baja Malibu.
I'll talk to your teacher if we have questions.

lista.es: ¿Me ==das== tu tabla si te ==aburres== de ella?
lista.en: Will you give me your board if you get bored of it?

lista.texto: **Cuando** takes the subjunctive for the future, **si** doesn't: [[5062|cuando]].
The future: [[5155|regular verbs in the future]].

lista.p: In Spanish: _If I have time, I'll train._
lista.r: Si tengo tiempo, entreno. / Si tengo tiempo, entrenaré.

lista.p: Fix it: **Si hará sol, vamos a la playa.**
lista.r: Si hace sol, vamos a la playa.
